  Independent H3 reviewer is tracing a possible wrong-checkout preflight: prepare_resume(root) hashes caller target/ci/hermit, batch run can actually
  execute fresh execution_root; post-run 4433 hashes actual execution_root. Please distinguish false refusals/usability from accepted mixed identities

  Searched for 1 pattern, listed 2 directories, ran 9 shell commands

● Verdict: changes requested. The round-3 commit makes resume and merge compare the recorded Hermit binary and test digests, and that comparison works.
  No changed check lowers the bar except one narrow, justified exemption (below). But H2 is still broken in the realistic case, and the resume pre-check
  hashes the wrong checkout's binary.

  Review target: hermit feat/pressure-test-resume-20261028, 4c98a7a0..5f28407ff0ed2ad410c03f9279baeb466c783dc8. Two files changed:
  ci/compat-envelope/pressure-test.rs (P below, +918/−20) and ci/manifest-plan/src/runner.rs (R below, which only makes test_digest pub).

  H3: should resume compare the hashes? Yes, and now it does

  - Where the hashes come from. R:9126-9153 records binary_sha256 as the SHA-256 of the file that actually ran (context.hermit_bin, which the cell
    command sets to HERMIT_BIN="$PWD/target/ci/hermit", P:151). It records test_sha256 as test_digest: the test's program source bytes, or the
    direct-command text (R:10261). R:9128-9132 also turns a binary that changed mid-cell into ERROR.
  - Resume. Rows without a recorded hash are refused (P:2516-2531). check_identities_against_current (P:2661-2697) refuses any row whose binary hash
    differs from the selected binary, or whose test is unknown or has a different current digest. It runs twice:
    - before execution, in prepare_resume (P:4566);
    - after execution, over every durable row, old and new, against the execution checkout's binary, before the summary is written (P:4429-4434).
  - Merge. All directories must share one binary hash, and one digest per test (P:3074-3104).
  - Is the old "no retained hash" waiver still there? No. The bar was not lowered.
  - Can mixed binaries be accepted? No such path found:
    - in-process resume is guarded by the post-run check;
    - merge enforces one binary across directories;
    - standalone summarize never uses the resume completion map once any resumed repetition is on disk (see H2), so it refuses rather than accepting
      mixed rows.
  - What the hashes do not cover:
    - test_sha256 identifies the source or command, not the built guest bytes.
    - binary_sha256 covers only target/ci/hermit. The DBT/LiteInst runtime .so files beside it, target/debug/test-harness, and host tools are not
      hashed. For those, the HEAD and clean-tree check is the only binding. That is a producer limit, not a lowered bar.

  Status of each round-2 finding

  Finding: H1 killed repetition reruns
  Status: Resolved
  Evidence and what remains: reset_in_progress_shell (P:2326-2332) runs after the rerun guard and before the 125 "incomplete" marker (P:8285-8287).
  Remaining edge: a kill between the rename and writing harness-status leaves 125 beside PASS rows. The new consistency check (P:2454-2481) then makes
  the whole resume fail until someone deletes that directory by hand. It does not just treat that repetition as missing. Fail-closed, low severity.
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Finding: H2 standalone summarize of a resumed run
  Status: Partially resolved (still broken in practice)
  Evidence and what remains: standalone_resume_completed (P:11773-11806) works out the completion map from the results that are on disk now. After a
  resume finishes, the repetitions it ran are on disk too, so the computed "still missing" set is empty while dag.json lists the resumed repetitions.
  It returns None (P:11800-11805), and the strict check refuses as in round 2. The self-test (P:18204-18245) never writes the resumed repetition's
  result (b rep 2), so it models only the state before execution. Fix: store the map from resume time (in run.json or the archive), or treat "full plan
   minus DAG jobs" as the completed set and require each of those to be on disk.
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Finding: H3 identity binding
  Status: Comparison resolved; the pre-check is partly wrong
  Evidence and what remains: prepare_resume(&root, …) runs at P:4245 (and in plan, P:4163) before the fresh checkout is made (P:4279-4290). It hashes
  the
  caller's working tree target/ci/hermit, and if that file is missing it runs cargo build there (P:2568-2620), even for plan. In batch mode the rows
  record the fresh checkout's binary, so the pre-check falsely refuses unless the two files are byte-identical. With a new fresh checkout, the build
  step rebuilds the binary (P:7419-7424). Hermit builds are not bit-reproducible, so the post-run check then refuses after the whole run. Exact-cell
  mode (execution root = working tree) is consistent. This wastes runs and refuses wrongly; it never accepts mixed binaries. Fix: hash the execution
  checkout in the pre-check. No test covers which checkout is used; the self-test calls the helpers directly (P:18040-18105).
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Finding: H4 merge hides failures
  Status: Resolved
  Evidence and what remains: Any non-PASS row keeps a repetition adverse, so ERROR/PASS can no longer be CLEAN in either order (P:3156-3157,
  P:3175-3182,
  merged_verdict P:2939). Out-of-range repetitions are refused (P:3065-3072). Reference cells with no rows now count as planned and show INCOMPLETE
  (P:2991-2993, P:3193-3197). Caveat: both need run.json; without it there is no plan to check against.
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Finding: M5 attempt provenance
  Status: Resolved, with nits
  Evidence and what remains: archive_resume_attempt keeps each earlier attempt in its own never-overwritten directory (P:4600-4624). Merge contributions

  now carry both hashes (P:2906-2907, P:3168-3169, P:3273-3274). Nits: unreadable files are skipped silently (if let Ok); plan  --resume, which only
  inspects, also creates archive directories; and a refused replan leaves an archive behind.
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Finding: M6 rollback before overwrite
  Status: Resolved
  Evidence and what remains: The snapshot and archive are taken before write_plan overwrites anything, and a failed write_plan restores them
  (P:4173-4188, P:4293-4308). dag.json is now written durably (P:8509). Restore errors are ignored (let _), but the archive still holds a durable copy.
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Finding: M8 legacy summarize exemption
  Status: Resolved
  Evidence and what remains: New plans set a durable_publication marker in run.json (P:3305, P:8527). Only runs without it keep the plain-rename
  exemption (P:8604-8606, P:9266). A new negative test refuses a marked run with a plain rename (P:17820-17843).
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Finding: M9 publish after failed fsync
  Status: Partially resolved
  Evidence and what remains: In-process: a failed directory fsync now undoes the publish (P:2291-2302). Shell form: the undo works only when the harness

  exited 0. The directory fsync now runs only if test "$status" -eq 0 (P:2314), and status already holds the harness exit (P:8292). So FAIL/ERROR
  repetitions skip the directory fsync completely, which round 2 always ran. That contradicts the help text at P:348. Impact is durability only: a
  crash leaves the repetition missing, never wrongly credited. Low severity.

  Goalpost-moving check

  - Assertions weakened: no. The self-test rows gained the hash fields (P:17296), which the new requirement needs. The retained-audit call now passes
    true explicitly, and a new refusal case was added (P:17818-17843).
  - Tolerance widened, exemption added, case skipped, or comparator relaxed: yes, one narrow case. On the resume path, validate_run_contract_with_resume
    skips the memory-requirement equality and the max-safe-width recompute (P:9161-9177). In-process this is harmless, because write_plan has just
    rebuilt run.json from the full plan. In a standalone summary those values are never re-checked; today H2's refusal stops that path being reached.
    The H3 waiver was removed and the legacy exemption was narrowed, so both of those tightened.
  - Failure relabelled as a pass: no. ERROR/PASS now stays adverse, and the harness-status consistency check rejects contradictions.
  - Check deleted instead of satisfied: no.
